scope: NYC 2026 recordings and primary written follow-ups; original attendee notes remain a historical record.
method: Screened 90 channel uploads, the NYC and online playlists, and the organizer's 52-session reading/transcript index. Selected transcripts were read substantively. Additional standalone releases were checked through official descriptions and chapter listings; their caption endpoints returned no usable text. No claim of audiovisual viewing or independent company-result verification is made.

records.mechanism: Vault joins time- and source-aware retrieval with an investor workbench and feedback into the research corpus. The transcript adds a roughly 200-question labeled relevance set and a reported precision@10 improvement from about 60% to 90–95%.
records.practice: Test eligible-source coverage separately from human-facing relevance; include plausible negatives and restrictive filters. Preserve information cutoff and access scope before synthesis.
records.limit: Internal retrieval results, without a disclosed held-out design or investment-performance estimate. The speaker corrects 'recall' to precision; the intended product direction is reactive resource to proactive participant.
records.title: Vault: Making Unstructured Data Work for Investing

records.mechanism: An agent registry makes ownership, purpose, tools, resources and risk visible. Scoped access and a separate approval path constrain execution; approval triage is a different responsibility from enforcement.
records.practice: Test a requested action at the enforcing boundary, including revocation, cross-user access and duplicate requests. Record which component can actually deny it.
records.limit: A described control framework is not a measured protection rate or proof that a triage classifier can waive required approval.
records.title: Balancing Acceleration and Safety for AI Agents

records.mechanism: Planners encode repeated work through Pick → Teach → Pack → Test → Ship. Skills retain reasons, clarification questions and stopping conditions. Each has an owner and a separate reviewer; agents send nothing to clients and professionals review recommendations.
records.practice: Start with a recognizable work product and previous cases. Test incomplete and conflicting inputs, then maintain the method as rules change.
records.limit: Five to ten cases is the speaker's practical starting suggestion, not statistical release assurance. Online recording is labeled October 13; attended notes place the session on October 14.
records.title: We Let Our Financial Planners Write the Agents
records.dateNote: Organizer livestream-index label, not an established filming date; standalone publication metadata is October 12.

records.mechanism: A tax-payment story spans client replies, approvals, trades and settlement. Shared workspaces retain plans and client context; tasks wake on events or deadlines instead of keeping a model reasoning continuously.
records.practice: Specify the waiting state, next event, responsible person and resumption condition for every handoff. Keep human approval and client communication explicit.
records.limit: The client narrative is an illustrative workflow, not a measured customer outcome. Use the financial-services firm identity introduced by the speaker.
records.title: Inside Arca’s long-horizon agents that run the business

records.mechanism: Language interpretation produces typed intent. A compiler validates a closed action vocabulary and can request clarification or refuse. Approved plans are immutable; approval binds the exact outgoing payload. An unknown side-effect outcome goes to manual review rather than blind retry.
records.practice: Distinguish failed, succeeded and outcome-unknown actions. Test changed payloads after approval and interruptions around external writes.
records.limit: Typed validity does not establish semantic correctness. Local-model routing examples are not measured fleetwide parity; the training feedback loop is described as future work.
records.title: Building Reliable, yet Smart Workflows for Finance, Wealth and Insurance
records.dateNote: Organizer livestream-index label, not an established filming date; standalone publication metadata is October 12.

records.mechanism: Frank Long decomposes external and internal context into decisions about selection, size and timing. Collection, filtering, extraction and cross-checking can use code, classical ML, language models or people.
records.practice: Give each step observable inputs, outputs and acceptance criteria. Use the appropriate executor for the step rather than maximizing the portion assigned to an LLM.
records.limit: A practitioner framework and worked scenario, not a disclosed autonomous fund or evidence of superior returns.
records.title: A Hedge Fund as a Function

records.mechanism: The strategy argument links problem selection, shared capabilities and compounding learning. Continuous evidence for or against an investment thesis is more decision-relevant than simply making summaries faster.
records.practice: Capture rejected approaches, definitions, known gaps and expert corrections in reusable team assets.
records.limit: The two contrasted firms are hypothetical; no employer or production result is inferred.
records.title: Everyone Has AI. Who Has the Advantage?

records.mechanism: The discussion prioritizes accessible data, repeatable evaluation and production controls while allowing models and scaffolding to change. Norm describes expert-labeled regression assets that made architecture comparisons possible.
records.practice: Preserve the acceptance dataset, semantic knowledge and protected operational primitives. Re-evaluate a model or harness change against equivalent work.
records.limit: Norm's evaluation assets belong to Norm's account. A shared panel does not establish a Blackstone deployment of every Norm component.
records.title: Built to Scale: Future-Proofing Your Technology Roadmap

records.mechanism: Structured-credit teams reconcile fragmented sources and definitions, prepare mock portfolios for PM refinement, and produce recurring financing/trade reports followed by team QA.
records.practice: Observe the actual analyst/operations workflow and determine why a feed is authoritative. Evaluate the reviewed artifact and correction effort.
records.limit: Reported days-to-minutes preparation examples lack a study protocol and full review-cost comparison. Draft completion is not an accuracy rate or a firmwide investment result.
records.title: AI in Practice: An Inside Look at Apollo's Approach

records.mechanism: A transformer is pretrained from scratch on transaction sequences, then adapted for fraud classification. Tokenizing amounts, categories, channels, time and location is central; the decision has a tight authorization-time latency budget.
records.practice: Choose representation and objective around the decision. Compare detection and false positives together with serving constraints.
records.limit: This is a transaction foundation model, not a proprietary language model. The reported improvement over XGBoost is not reproducible from the transcript alone.
records.title: Wells Fargo Foundation Model: Application to Fraud Detection at Scale

records.mechanism: Separate source selection, exact fact retrieval and arithmetic. Models plan with fact identifiers while code resolves facts and computes; direct reads and search both respect access boundaries. Final post-processing is still needed because generation can invent a number afterward.
records.practice: Check entity, period, unit, source version, calculation and final rendered claim separately. Unsupported claims must be removed, corrected or escalated.
records.limit: No zero-hallucination guarantee follows from pointer lookup. This main-stage follow-up is distinct from the attended 'Do Not Let Models Invent Numbers' breakout.
records.title: Why Wall Street Still Doesn’t Trust AI

records.mechanism: Observation, storage, decision definitions and model assumptions impose different schemas. Examples retain row counts while dates disappear, categories change or negative signs lose meaning. Multiple models can share the same wrong convention.
records.practice: Version decision-specific definitions and test typed intermediate fields: signs, nulls, dates, categories, grain and join coverage. Agreement is a diagnostic signal, not independent truth.
records.limit: Task examples support semantic checks, not a universal claim that schemas or ensembles always succeed or fail.
records.title: Just-in-Time Ontologies

records.mechanism: Institutional memory updates and ages beliefs, observes contradictions, grades past predictions and accepts corrections. Reported status and evidence-based status remain separate; historical snapshots are preserved. Models propose updates, while code and people commit them.
records.practice: Store evidence time, origin, source health and correction history. Missing telemetry is unknown, not zero. Backtest as-of snapshots against later observations without rewriting history.
records.limit: The reported associations are observational. Client-franchise expansion is a direction, not an established completed capability.
records.title: Your Company Has No Model of Itself: Bootstrapping a World Model from Slack, Decks and Meetings

records.mechanism: The finance product discussion links data access, inspectable source passages/tables, charts and reusable work artifacts. A useful answer must fit the professional's existing output and review process.
records.practice: Test the exported document as well as the chat response: values, periods, units, provenance and corrections must survive into the artifact.
records.limit: Product description and forward-looking agent capabilities do not establish universal availability, entitlements or measured financial accuracy. Uncertain provider spelling in the attendee notes is not guessed.
records.title: Building the Next Chapter of AI in Finance

records.mechanism: Shared deal threads, an agent inbox and Office-like artifact engines support longer analyst work. Authorization has to follow participants and sources; write–render–check–fix connects reasoning to a usable document.
records.practice: Assess source breadth, workbook depth, participant access and exported-artifact fidelity as separate requirements.
records.limit: Vendor architecture and ambition, not verified full Office parity or investment success. The founder's prior Coatue role does not establish current Coatue deployment.
records.title: Towards Autonomous Analysts in Finance

records.mechanism: Fully acceptable work and average rubric credit measure different things. Historical issue replay starts from the repository state before the known resolution; benchmark validity, repeatability and discrimination matter alongside gaming controls.
records.practice: Replay accepted historical work with its original inputs and allowed tools. Report complete acceptance and diagnostic dimensions separately.
records.limit: The reported spending reduction is an internal experiment; free token credits are not a paid bill or transferable ROI.
records.title: Beyond the Model Card: The Jagged Frontier of AI in Finance

records.mechanism: A reconciliation can reach zero variance through an unsupported adjustment and still be wrong. Behavior specs first ask whether a situation occurred, then whether the agent acted appropriately. Forks isolate a decision; cheaper simulations test repair hypotheses.
records.practice: Record applicable / not applicable separately from pass / fail. Allow an explained discrepancy rather than rewarding a fabricated balancing entry. Reproduce promising simulated repairs in the real environment.
records.limit: Agent explanations are clues, not proven causes. The fork is an illustrated repair, not a measured general success rate; outcome evaluations remain necessary.
records.title: Process Supervision for Agents That Do Long-Horizon Work

records.mechanism: A frontier orchestrator can delegate a narrow financial task to a specialized model. Prepared context cartridges are exploratory; parallel security work separates search, deduplication and reproduction.
records.practice: Identify the bottleneck and its task-specific score before specializing. Keep production, experiment and roadmap claims separate within the same talk.
records.limit: This keynote is not Ryan Stevens's skill/memory breakout. Its task scores and security findings do not establish general superiority or universal retry reliability.
records.title: Chasing capabilities while waiting for the frontier

records.mechanism: Each case combines task, synthetic business world, trajectory and accountant-authored rubric. The account reports eight-to-four skill ablation (+2.8 mean-score points across six worlds), 61% spreadsheet-skill compression with essentially unchanged quality, and trajectory-distilled memory (+5.7 points over skills alone).
records.practice: Advance the same business one period, remove prior-period amounts from memory and evaluate next-period work. Compare per-world regressions as well as the average.
records.limit: Written primary account, not a located breakout recording or independently reproduced benchmark. Point gains are not relative percentages or a forecast for another team.
records.title: Ramp · Ryan Stevens written follow-up

records.mechanism: A disposable sandbox receives temporary repository/credential access; issue history, useful skills and run telemetry persist outside it. Replacement runs can resume from durable progress. Human-labeled data calibrates evaluators before use.
records.practice: Separate the lifetime of task state from the lifetime of execution authority. Trace the agents modifying the system as well as those serving users.
records.limit: Proposed fixes/PRs and regression evaluation do not establish safe autonomous production release or measured diagnostic accuracy.
records.title: What does an AI engineer do?

records.mechanism: The transcript emphasizes intent, preventive constraints, independent verification and repeatable release evidence. The creation/release/operation three-loop teaching structure also draws on the prior agenda and our synthesis.
records.practice: Provide low-noise checks at generation time, broader release tests and reproduction of escaped failures. Maintain an accountable promotion/rollback decision.
records.limit: The confidence product is conceptual. The 50k-line code-translation example is not a universal limit; survey sentiment and vendor results are not independently verified defect reductions.
records.title: The Machine that Changed the World, vAI

records.mechanism: Software disposability depends on consequences, dependencies, replacement cost and maintenance burden. The constructive response is also to make rigor cheaper through shared tests, fakes, standards and fast feedback.
records.practice: Revisit a tool's rigor when users, consequences or dependencies grow. Build the shortest dependable path, including checks, rather than deferring verification.
records.limit: A conceptual engineering argument, not evidence that Capital One deployed a particular disposable-software program.
records.title: Does Code Quality Even Matter?

records.mechanism: A forward-moving policy workflow can contain bounded draft/check/refine loops. A policy-checkable result authorizes leaving a node; human review and escalation remain explicit.
records.practice: Define entry, acceptance, iteration budget and takeover conditions for each stage. Reduce supervision only when representative evidence supports the change.
records.limit: Framework and examples, not evidence that every illustrated process runs autonomously at Coinbase. Thresholds shown are not portable safety constants.
records.title: Trusting Agents in Policy-Driven Workflows

records.mechanism: Registration, workload identity, a tool gateway, checkpoints and run/trajectory records form a production platform. Context preparation selects/prunes, reranks, deduplicates and compresses; an Artifactory demo reports 24,000 to 2,400 tokens.
records.practice: Evaluate required-fact coverage and final quality alongside tokens, latency and review. Redact before model calls and before memory/trace persistence.
records.limit: A token-use demo does not establish equivalent answer quality, general latency improvement or a production-wide savings rate.
records.title: Paving the Road to Production: Governed Enterprise AI Agents

records.mechanism: Agent defenses combine short-lived scoped identities, deterministic tool-call checks, tenant isolation, default-deny egress including DNS, and budgets that halt. Persistent memory can retain injected instructions.
records.practice: Test enforcement with denied actions and cross-tenant requests. Treat external documents as data, review memory writes, and verify that stop controls actually stop.
records.limit: Incident stories motivate defenses; this review does not independently verify incidents or treat a control checklist as complete protection.
records.title: Security in the Age of AI: Recent Attacks, Incidents & Defenses

records.mechanism: Delivery cost combines human salary and AI spend per merged PR. The reported observational comparison includes lower unit cost despite a much larger token bill, with reverts and change size as counterchecks.
records.practice: Translate the denominator to accepted work in your domain and include review, rework, failures and operation. Monitor quality beside throughput.
records.limit: Merged PRs are a proxy, not full business value. Association between higher use and better economics does not prove that spending more causes improvement.
records.title: Tokens Are the Cheap Part

records.mechanism: Corrections and repeated workflows can become owned evaluation assets. A proposed progression moves from workflow discovery and skills to evaluation, routing and, when justified, specialized training.
records.practice: Retain adjudicated examples, task versions and expert corrections before optimizing the implementation. Require an independent acceptance standard for a smaller-model comparison.
records.limit: Organization-wide continuous training is forward-looking. Agreement with a stronger model is not sufficient ground truth.
records.title: Self-Improving Organizations

records.mechanism: The release describes live research comparisons, cost per useful insight, timing agents that revisit older ideas and the hidden cost of fixing tools. Chapter markers locate those topics for review.
records.practice: Predefine useful insight and track decision timing, human effort and repairs, rather than relying on an attractive ROI title.
records.limit: No usable caption text was recovered. Randomization, controls, sample size and causal alpha remain unverified; description supplements the original attendee notes.
records.title: Proving Alpha: How a Hedge Fund Measures AI's ROI - Hari Kumar, Contour Asset Management

records.mechanism: The standalone release describes a citation registry, deterministic calculation, hybrid retrieval, tenant isolation and typed facts with value, unit, scale and period. Chapters separate retrieval, verification and the limits of guarantees.
records.practice: Use the source's exact fact structure to organize review, then test semantic selection and final output independently.
records.limit: Description/chapter evidence only for this edition. Its 20:58 duration and contents differ from the October 14 main-stage follow-up; exact retrieval settings are not adopted as defaults.
records.title: Do Not Let Models Invent Numbers - Vinoo Ganesh, Kepler

records.mechanism: A described prompt repair improves safety while reducing task completion. The regression loop curates trace-derived datasets, scores, establishes a baseline, compares a change and gates merges.
records.practice: Keep a vector of consequential scores and paired regressions instead of declaring a fix successful from one improved number.
records.limit: No transcript recovered; the described tradeoff is a teaching example, not an externally verified performance estimate.
records.title: Your Agent Fix Just Broke Something Else - Sofia Jakovcevic, Arize AI

records.mechanism: The product-engineer argument follows bottlenecks from code creation to review, operations and security. Discovering what users need and defining good work remain central responsibilities.
records.practice: Interview users in their real workflow, define acceptance, inspect delivered artifacts and measure whether the bottleneck moved.
records.limit: Description-level scope. Hiring statistics and productivity multipliers are not imported as independently checked findings.
records.title: AI Writes the Code. So What's Left for Engineers? - Laurie Voss, Arize AI

records.mechanism: A Slack entry point combines with an internal MCP gateway, sandboxed orchestration and a reusable agent building block for coding, incidents and other requests.
records.practice: Treat discovery, tools, identity and supported execution as product capabilities. Measure accepted outputs and reviewer burden separately from task volume.
records.limit: Reported task/PR adoption is not coding quality, net productivity or a causal savings result; transcript text was not recovered.
records.title: A Bank Built Its Own Coding Agent. It Took Off — Felippe Felisola Caso & Francesco Galletta, Monzo

records.mechanism: The release concerns cash-ledger modernization and making legacy code queryable through MCP. The seven-days-to-fifteen-minutes comparison is mainframe-code research, alongside data, producer and consumer migration.
records.practice: Make legacy definitions and migration documentation accessible, preserve observability, and assess financial invariants through the change.
records.limit: The title does not describe investment research. Task timing is a speaker claim without a full cost/quality study; total migration benefit cannot be attributed to AI alone.
records.title: AI Cut Our Research Time From 7 Days to 15 Minutes — Gareth Yoder, Vanguard

records.mechanism: MandateBench is presented as a task from fund mandate to investment memo, contrasting full analyst work with narrow finance questions. The release also describes reproducibility and benchmark-gaming problems.
records.practice: Preserve allowed resources, evaluator integrity, repeated-run variability and the actual professional acceptance criteria.
records.limit: No usable transcript or inspected benchmark dataset in this review. Specific benchmark failure rates and early results are not reproduced as validated findings.
records.title: Why Frontier Models Fail as Buy-Side Analysts - Janie Gu, Google DeepMind & Suyeol Yun, LinqAlpha

records.mechanism: The described answer-first method specifies an expected result, creates inputs containing the needed evidence and tests recovery. Candidate fixtures include past decisions, planted violations, removed clauses and meaning-preserving edits.
records.practice: Keep a known answer and validate the generated evidence. Add missing-evidence and invariant-preserving cases; have experts inspect realism and answer-key correctness.
records.limit: Description-level method. A daily-testing improvement refers to a past telecom example, not an established Air Canada contract-agent result.
records.title: How to Test AI Agents When No Benchmark Exists — Nathanael Weill, Air Canada

records.mechanism: The release emphasizes representative local tasks, repeated experiments, complete traces and gates that actually stop work. Observe execution independently rather than trusting an agent-authored success record.
records.practice: Fix the harness and environment when comparing models. Verify actual tool effects and immutable grading inputs; retain full task evidence.
records.limit: The described 30% change has an unspecified percent scale and task population; no portable effect size is adopted.
records.title: Don't Trust Your AI Agents. Test Them Like a Scientist — Stephanie Jarmak, Omni Analytics

records.company: Failure study · New York Life affiliation
records.mechanism: The description organizes selected public incidents around technical strength, deployment controls and business impact, and motivates failure-driven tests plus evaluation of the evaluators themselves.
records.practice: Use incident mechanisms to build adversarial and regression cases. Separate materiality from frequency, and inspect false passes in the grader.
records.limit: Coverage of a selected incident database is not population incidence or proof of causation. The original expected-loss equation and insurer-wide deployment remain unverified.
records.title: 1,368 AI Failures and What They Teach About Evals — Vishal Srivastava, New York Life & Tanmay Sah
